synopsis: Forum user reported an EVO Max 4T disconnect during search and rescue training that ended in return to home.
narrative: During a search and rescue training flight, about five minutes into the third sortie at roughly 188 ft height and 682 ft distance with 29 satellites, the EVO Max 4T's camera feed became erratic and stopped responding, the screen greyed out and a disconnection warning appeared. The aircraft eventually began return to home. About 40 seconds later the pilot regained control but had no camera feed, and landed normally. The poster later said they received replacement controllers, still saw issues mainly after hot-swapping batteries, and watched for a slowly pulsing controller signal-strength indicator as a warning sign.

synopsis: Forum user reported an EVO Max 4T flyaway in which return to home had no effect.
narrative: An EVO Max 4T owner reported a flyaway on 11 November about two minutes into a flight at a familiar desert site with more than 18 satellites. The aircraft stopped responding to control inputs and pressing return to home changed nothing; it kept flying away in a direction different from the takeoff point, and video and connection were lost. The owner said Autel's analysis found nothing wrong with the aircraft and the replacement request was unresolved.

synopsis: Second forum user reported an EVO Max 4T climbing past its altitude limit after commanding return to home during a mission.
narrative: A second EVO Max 4T user ran a waypoint mission with the controller's maximum altitude set to 399 ft and return-to-home altitude to 328 ft, with 21 satellites. About 700 ft out the aircraft stopped and hovered as if stuck. When the user commanded it home it began to return but then climbed to about 755 ft, and the app showed a maximum-altitude warning. The excerpt does not give the final outcome.
